asset_explanations.summary: Figure 2 illustrates the HACL framework and its two-stage training paradigm. Panel (b) outlines the training process: Stage 1 involves text generation and intra-LLM contrastive learning, while Stage 2 focuses on self-instruction tuning.

supported_claims.claim: LLaVA without contrastive learning or hallucinative captions achieves a POPE F1 score of 66.48.

asset_explanations.caption: Figure 4. This figure illustrates the visualization of various data distributions. The blue icons represent visual data extracted from images, the green icons denote ground truth caption data, and the red icons signify hallucinative caption data. The label "w/o HACL" represents the data distribution obtained from the original model output without employing our proposed method. On the other hand, "w/ CL" indicates the data distribution resulting from the model output utilizing contrastive learning. Lastly, "w/ HACL" indicates the data distribution generated by the model output using our proposed method.
asset_explanations.summary: Figure 4 displays three 3D scatter plots visualizing data distributions in a latent space defined by PC1, PC2, and PC3. The plots compare the alignment of visual data (blue dots), ground truth captions (green circles), and hallucinative captions (red triangles) under three conditions: without the proposed method (w/o HACL), with contrastive learning (w/ CL), and with the proposed method (w/ HACL). Panel (a) shows a clear separation between visual data and text data. Panel (b) shows all data types heavily overlapped. Panel (c) shows visual data separated from text data, but with ground truth data positioned closer to visual data than hallucinative data, suggesting the proposed method distinguishes hallucinations.
